commands.command: Python SHA-256 comparison of R candidate

verified_contracts: Actual RV64 process parses the manifest, reads sources in order, lexically scans, and writes exact concatenated bytes; empty inputs and multi-buffer inputs pass.
Injected providers force seven-byte I/O and EINTR; target code performs retry and byte-copy loops. The host only supplies fixture inputs and checks outputs.
Independent second-source-missing probe checks removal after a preceding source has already been written.
Independent dangling-output-symlink probe confirms O_EXCL rejection preserves the existing symlink and does not create its target.
Independent final-output-close failure probe closes fd 3 then returns an error after data was written; target exits 13 and removes new output.

Target parser rejects source/assembly path duplication; scanner accepts UTF-8 comments/string bytes while rejecting unsupported identifier bytes; precise token/error offsets verified by target library test.
Direct image and Clang/LLD reference execute the same target source and produce identical output bytes.
limitations: Runtime is Linux-user and bounded by static BSS buffers; no heap allocator, SOS adapter or self-compilation is claimed.
ASCII target manifest separators and ASCII identifiers are documented restrictions; numeric token semantic validation remains future parser work.
Cleanup invokes close/unlink; this does not establish crash durability or guarantee unlink succeeds when the environment refuses removal.
Project CLI integration, atomic executable publication, unused extern provider resolution and clean-build evidence belong to I.
